title_original: Cannes Chief Thierry Fremaux Hails French Film Model as CNC Head Gaëtan Bruel Vows to Fight for Its Future at 80th Anniversary

article_text:
France’s National Film Board , the CNC, marked its 80th anniversary with a three-day gathering of industry leaders in Paris, including Cannes Film Festival chief Thierry Frémaux who praised the country’s unique film funding system. CNC president Gaëtan Bruel, meanwhile, warned against attempts to dismantle a model that has helped make France a global cinema powerhouse.

The anniversary celebrations, held from Oct. 26-28 at the Cinémathèque française, came at a particularly fraught moment for the institution which faces growing political scrutiny and budgetary pressures as France heads toward the 2027 presidential election.

Queer Bodybuilder Drama 'Test' Acquired by Dark Star Pictures (EXCLUSIVE)

Frémaux, who also heads the Institut Lumière in Lyon, highlighted the CNC’s key role on display across films showcased at Cannes and other major festivals.

“We don’t say it because the Americans accuse us of constantly favoring certain things, because they themselves cannot imagine that the selection process is conducted in complete independence. But you can see just how much French money, the CNC and French professionals are absolutely everywhere,” Frémaux said during an onstage conversation with film historian Antoine de Baecque at the French Cinémathèque on Wednesday.

Frémaux also pointed out the CNC’s support for film restoration, noting that countries around the world have begun developing similar initiatives.

“Every country in the world has its masterpieces. And not all masterpieces have been restored, so there is still plenty of work to be done. Many countries are now giving themselves the means to do this, following the French model,” he said.

Frémaux emphasized that France’s film funding system not only supports contemporary production but also helps preserve cinema’s history and nurture future generations of film lovers.

“People are finally beginning to understand that money from cinema goes back into cinema. It has taken a long time, but I’m starting to read things about it. Journalists are always a little slow,” he joked. “But the fact remains that this money from cinema also goes toward cinema’s history. And that brings us back to the fundamental role of building an educational and intellectual foundation for cinephilia as a driving force in protecting contemporary creation.”

The event wrapped with a forceful defense of the institution from Bruel, who took over as CNC president last year and is facing pressures from populist parties, including the far right party Rassemblement National. In its latest budget proposal, unveiled earlier this month, the party outlined plans to strip down the National Film Board, privatize public broadcasting and slash public broadcasting funding

“We are going through, on a global scale, one of the deepest crises this sector has experienced since the invention of cinema,” Bruel said. “These 80 years have not been a smooth ride. They have been marked by successive upheavals. But what we are experiencing today is as though we were facing the ocean head-on, as though the upheavals of eight decades were happening all at once.”

Bruel also pointed to the industry’s shifting power dynamics, as streaming platforms are now facing new competition from YouTube.

“A few years ago, streamers seemed to be triumphing over television and movie theaters. Today, faced with YouTube, they themselves are discovering their vulnerabilities, and they are seeking to converge with traditional broadcasters, a sign that yesterday’s world has not said its last word,” he said.

For Bruel, these changes make the CNC’s mission more important than ever, particularly as public support for the arts faces increasing criticism.

“According to some, the CNC is a dispensable appendage, and all we would need to do is cut it off to get better. You can always cut off an arm, but you’d better be sure of what you stand to gain and what you stand to lose,” he said.

Bruel argued that France’s film funding model also serves a civic role, in giving people access to culture, through an extensive network of movie theaters, as well as film education programs allowing an estimated two million schoolchildren to visit movie theater each year.

The CNC’s 80th anniversary brought together a broad cross-section of France’s film and television industries for three days of discussions exploring the institution’s history and its evolving role in the entertainment landscape.

Among the prominent filmmakers participating were Olivier Assayas, Arnaud Desplechin, Amélie Bonnin and Rachid Hami, alongside producers Anne-Dominique Toussaint, Alex Berger and Simone Harari Baulieu, and leading animation executives including Illumination Studios Paris co-founder Jacques Bled and Xilam Animation founder Marc du Pontavice.

The program explored the defense of theatrical exhibition, the rise of French animation, the expansion of the CNC’s remit into television, video games and immersive creation, and the challenges posed by Hollywood’s global dominance. A panel devoted to protecting movie theaters featured Desplechin alongside exhibitors Aurélie Delage and Camille Labé, and former UGC chief Alain Sussfeld. Another discussion examined the CNC’s expansion into television, bringing together Berger, Harari Baulieu, former CNC director general and Arte president Jérôme Clément, and screenwriter-director Clémence Madeleine-Perdrillat.

Looking ahead, Bruel signaled that the CNC would soon present a broader strategy for digital creators and social media platforms like YouTube, arguing that they should contribute more fairly to the financing of French audiovisual creation, on par with streaming services.

His words on investment alluded to the European Commission’s current review of the Audiovisual Media Service Directive which allows members states to require streaming platforms such as Netflix, Disney+ and Prime Video to invest in European film and television production. The review could also open the door to bringing YouTube under similar investment obligations to level the playing field between broadcasters, streamers and digital platforms.

“Will we remain one in the future? No battle is lost in advance, especially when we have so many strengths in our hands, and you can count on the CNC to play its full part. But the answer, by definition, remains open,” Bruel concluded.

article_text:
Several new challengers are stepping into the box office ring this weekend to face off.

Paramount and Legendary’s “ Street Fighter ” video game adaptation should lead the pack of newcomers. It made $4 million in Thursday previews at the box office, and it’s expected to make $25 million to $35 million in its debut. Legendary and video game developer Capcom co-financed the film for $82 million, and it’s the first release under Paramount’s global distribution deal with Legendary. Directed by Kitao Sakura, the new take on the classic fighting games star Noah Centineo, Andrew Koji, Callina Liang, Jason Momoa, 50 Cent and more as colorful brawlers who face off in a high-stakes tournament.

Related Stories

'Slow Horses' Director on Season 6 and That Final Jack Lowden Scene: 'We Had Two Endings and One of Them Was Happy'

‘Killing a Bear,’ From Movistar Plus and Arte France: a Real-Event Inspired Murder-Mystery Whose Victim Is a Pyrenean Brown Bear

Disney’s “ Whalefall ” made $900,000 in Thursday previews and is looking to claim second place with $10 million to $12 million this weekend. Directed by Brian Duffield, it stars Austin Abrams as a scuba diver who gets swallowed by a giant sperm whale and must find a way to escape. It cost $60 million to produce, but positive reviews for the claustrophobic thriller should give it some staying power.

Popular on Variety

The highly anticipated Elizabeth Holmes documentary “ You Can See Everything ” from A24 made $1.75 million in previews and is aiming for third place with $7 million to $8 million, a stellar debut for a non-fiction doc. The movie cost just $7 million to produce and has been building hype since it had a surprise debut at last month’s Telluride Film Festival. Directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim secretly filmed Elizabeth Holmes ahead of her 11-year prison sentence and even lived with the disgraced Theranos founder to get full access to her life. It’s expected to be a rare box office hit for a documentary and could even land in this year’s Oscar race.

The final newcomer this weekend is Focus Features’ Jane Austen adaptation of “ Sense and Sensibility ,” which cost $25 million and is on track to make $5 million to $8 million this weekend. It made $1.15 million from advance screenings and previews. The new take on the classic novel stars Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles as Elinor and Marianne Dashwood, who navigate love, loss and financial uncertainty as they are forced to leave their family estate in Sussex.

article_text:
煙突の中の雀

劇場公開日： 2026年10月30日

映画館を探す

予告編を見る

U-NEXTで 関連作品を見る PR

解説・あらすじ

スイス出身の双子の映画作家ラモン＆シルバン・チュルヒャー兄弟の長編第3作で、長編デビュー作「ストレンジ・リトル・キャット」および第2作「ガール・アンド・スパイダー」に続く「動物三部作」の第3作。 カレンは幼少期を過ごした森のほとりの家で、夫や子どもたちと暮らしている。夫の誕生日を祝うため、社交的な姉ユーレが家族を伴って訪ねてくるが、ユーレにとってこの家は強権的だった亡き母との不快な思い出に満ちた場所だった。やがて、それぞれが抱えるわだかまりやトラウマが次々と表面化し、家族の均衡が徐々に崩れていく。 ラモンが監督・脚本・編集を手がけ、シルバンが製作を担当。「アイム・ユア・マン 恋人はアンドロイド」のマレン・エッゲルトがカレン役で主演を務め、「落下音」のルイーゼ・ハイヤーが謎めいた女性リフを演じた。2024年・第37回東京国際映画祭「ユース」部門および2025年・第26回東京フィルメックス上映作品。2026年10月には「ストレンジ・リトル・キャット」「ガール・アンド・スパイダー」とともに、「ミニアチュールの詩学 チュルヒャー兄弟『動物三部作』」と題して劇場公開。

2024年製作／117分／PG12／スイス 原題または英題：Der Spatz im Kamin 配給：グッチーズ・フリースクール 劇場公開日：2026年10月30日

"战士阿周那刚刚开始祈祷，就遭遇了一幕如此令人震惊的景象，吓得他连忙抓起弓箭。在他面前站着一个由九种动物部件组成的奇美拉。阿周那瞄准目标，但当他注意到野兽的人类手中有一朵莲花——黑天神的标志时，他停了下来。这个神圣的生物象征着真理具有多面性，有时难以完全看透，却在万物和每个人身上都有所折射。这个寓言反映了“现代跨地方系列：纠缠与交织”背后的价值观，该展览由四位韩国艺术家和四位印度艺术家在彼此国家进行研究交流后创作的纺织品委任作品组成。他们顶住日益高涨的仇外情绪，对所接触的工艺传统的关注，最终呈现出一个在技术造诣上令人眩目、在过去与现在文化联系的故事中引人入胜的展览。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "纳万贡贾拉（Navangunjara）——出现在阿周那面前的这个生物——是诗人萨拉拉·达萨（Sarala Dasa）用奥迪亚语对《摩诃婆罗多》15世纪重述中所独有的。来自奥迪沙邦的艺术与时尚集体 Boito 创作了一尊纳万贡贾拉雕塑，其每个部分都代表着当地的一种工艺：例如，它的孔雀颈上覆盖着布面帕塔契特拉（pattachitra）绘画，而编织的萨巴伊草（sabai grass）则构成了它的蛇尾。同样参考15世纪史诗的张延顺（Yeonsoon Chang）的“月映千川”系列（2025年）意为“月亮倒映在千条河流上”。这一佛教教义呼应了真理并非单一、而是呈现多种形式的观念。为了这件装置，张延顺将靛蓝染色的蕉麻织物缝制并熨烫成近乎棱柱状的结构，从而营造出光的渐变，让人联想到投射在水面上的月光。靛蓝同样为 Kaimurai 的作品着色，他将这种颜料视为神圣，并在冥想的过程中画出密集的放射状线条。摆放在附近的是曼彻斯特惠特沃思美术馆藏品中一件19世纪的靛蓝防染棉布，它呼应了欧洲历史上对“蓝金”的需求。由于广受欢迎，靛蓝在印度被广泛种植，常常取代粮食作物。农民最终在1859年的靛蓝起义中奋起反抗殖民地种植园主。这件残片 exemplify 了博物馆藏品中深思熟虑的纳入如何使展览的物质历史变得复杂。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/Yeonsoon-Chang-Worincheongang-I-IV-1.jpg", "alt": "", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "PÉRO 的", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "纠缠的记忆，交织的故事，2025年（右），摄于曼彻斯特惠特沃思美术馆“现代跨地方系列：纠缠与交织”，2026年。摄影：迈克尔·波拉德（Michael Pollard）。惠特沃思美术馆提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "苏马克希·辛格（Sumakshi Singh）的《跨越虚空》（2025年）延伸了精神对称的主题，用精致的花边重现了清州的一座桥梁。这些错综复杂的游丝状线迹复制了桥梁的木质纹理以及其栅栏中嵌入的卐字纹，后者诉说着佛教沿丝绸之路从印度向东亚的传播。在柳贞惠（Jounghye Yoo）的装置中可以找到另一件宗教建筑。这些薄如蝉翼的织物层——带有金色刺绣图案以及阿杰拉克（Ajrakh）手版印花和防染图案——被剪裁得酷似瓦拉纳西维斯瓦纳特寺（Vishwanath Temple）的大门。与辛格和柳贞惠一样，时尚品牌 Péro 运用纺织品的语言来重新诠释围绕人体展开的建筑形式。《纠缠的记忆，交织的故事》（2015–25年）完全由通常用于闭合服装缝线和毛边的针脚组成，让人想起莫卧儿宫殿的格子屏风。其精细的线艺类似于惠特沃思美术馆藏品中一张图案华丽的奇坎卡里（Chikankari）垫子。这件文物再次揭示了殖民历史。白底白花的奇坎卡里刺绣在莫卧儿时期发展起来，在英国统治下因不敌工业化制造的纺织品而走向衰落。它作为一种民间艺术得以存活下来，在以微薄生计维系的女性之间代代相传。", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“现代跨地方系列：交织与编织”（Hyundai Translocal Series: Entangled and Woven）展览现场，左侧为洪英仁（Young In Hong）作品《神圣帝国》（Sacred Empires，2025年），右侧为其《雪中白鹤》（White Cranes in Snowfall，2024年），展于曼彻斯特惠特沃斯美术馆（the Whitworth），2026年。摄影：Michael Pollard。图片由惠特沃斯美术馆提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "工薪阶层女性的工艺在洪荣仁的《神圣帝国》（2025年）中成为焦点。这一系列旗帜是与库奇（Kutch）的卡拉·拉克沙（Kala Raksha）集体共同制作的，在那里，不同的刺绣和镜面刺绣风格被作为社区的鲜明标志而受到赞誉。这些拼布旗帜点缀着精致的圆形镜子和充满活力的针脚，代表了动物群落及其流动的领地，将身份定位为既是内在的又是响应性的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "高素美（Somi Ko）的《People of One, Moment》（2025年）中也出现了镜面刺绣。在这里，闪闪发光的圆片排列在五块棉质展板上，呈现出舞蹈人物的形状。这些狂喜的瞬间揭示了一个真理：我们的内心里都映照着彼此，因此，我们互为彼此最好的老师。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "朱颖（Chloe Chu）是一位常驻伦敦的艺术撰稿人兼编辑。", "translated": true}]

Photo by Wooil Kim. Copyright the Cheongju Craft Biennale Organizing Committee. Courtesy the Whitworth."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Hyundai Translocal Series: Entangled and Woven The Whitworth Manchester Jul 10, 2026–Jan 3, 2027"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The warrior Arjuna had just settled into prayer when he was confronted by a sight so shocking it sent him scrambling for his bow and arrow. Before him stood a chimera composed of nine animal parts. Arjuna took aim but stopped when he noticed a lotus flower—Lord Krishna’s emblem—in the beast’s human hand. The divine creature symbolizes how truth is multifaceted, at times challenging to wholly behold, but inflected in everything and everyone. The parable reflects the values behind “Hyundai Translocal Series: Entangled and Woven,” which comprised textile-based commissions developed by four South Korean artists and four Indian artists following research exchanges in one another’s countries. Challenging rising xenophobic tides, their attentiveness to the craft traditions they encountered resulted in a presentation as dazzling in its technical prowess as it was compelling in its stories of past and present cultural connections."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The Navangunjara—the being that appeared to Arjuna—is unique to poet Sarala Dasa’s 15th-century retelling of the Mahabharata in the Odia language. Hailing from Odisha state, the art-and-fashion collective Boito created a sculpture of the Navangunjara, with each part representing a local craft: its peacock neck, for example, is covered in cloth-based pattachitra paintings, while plaited sabai grass forms its serpent tail. Similarly referencing a 15th-century epic poem, the title of Yeonsoon Chang’s Worincheongang series (2025) translates as “the moon reflected on a thousand rivers.” The Buddhist teaching echoes the notion that truth is not singular but takes diverse forms. For the installation, Chang sewed and ironed indigo-dyed abacá fabric into almost prismatic structures that create gradients of light, evoking moonlight cast on water. Indigo likewise colors the work of Kaimurai, who considers the pigment sacred and paints dense, radial lines in a meditative process. article_text:
Shows

“Entangled and Woven” at the Whitworth

KAIMURAI ’s

The answers to all my prayers are in the questions I never asked , 2025, natural indigo on handwoven unbleached fabric, bronze bell, veena string, chiseled granite sphere, dimensions variable, at “Hyundai Translocal Series: Entangled and Woven,” the Whitworth, Manchester, 2026. Photo by Wooil Kim. Copyright the Cheongju Craft Biennale Organizing Committee. Courtesy the Whitworth.

Hyundai Translocal Series: Entangled and Woven The Whitworth Manchester Jul 10, 2026–Jan 3, 2027

The warrior Arjuna had just settled into prayer when he was confronted by a sight so shocking it sent him scrambling for his bow and arrow. Before him stood a chimera composed of nine animal parts. Arjuna took aim but stopped when he noticed a lotus flower—Lord Krishna’s emblem—in the beast’s human hand. The divine creature symbolizes how truth is multifaceted, at times challenging to wholly behold, but inflected in everything and everyone. The parable reflects the values behind “Hyundai Translocal Series: Entangled and Woven,” which comprised textile-based commissions developed by four South Korean artists and four Indian artists following research exchanges in one another’s countries. Challenging rising xenophobic tides, their attentiveness to the craft traditions they encountered resulted in a presentation as dazzling in its technical prowess as it was compelling in its stories of past and present cultural connections.

The Navangunjara—the being that appeared to Arjuna—is unique to poet Sarala Dasa’s 15th-century retelling of the Mahabharata in the Odia language. Hailing from Odisha state, the art-and-fashion collective Boito created a sculpture of the Navangunjara, with each part representing a local craft: its peacock neck, for example, is covered in cloth-based pattachitra paintings, while plaited sabai grass forms its serpent tail. Similarly referencing a 15th-century epic poem, the title of Yeonsoon Chang’s Worincheongang series (2025) translates as “the moon reflected on a thousand rivers.” The Buddhist teaching echoes the notion that truth is not singular but takes diverse forms. For the installation, Chang sewed and ironed indigo-dyed abacá fabric into almost prismatic structures that create gradients of light, evoking moonlight cast on water. Indigo likewise colors the work of Kaimurai, who considers the pigment sacred and paints dense, radial lines in a meditative process. Placed nearby was a piece of 19th-century indigo resist-dyed cotton from the Whitworth’s collection in Manchester, nodding to the historical demand for “blue gold” in Europe. Because of its popularity, indigo was widely cultivated in India, often in place of food crops. Farmers eventually rose against colonial planters in the Indigo Revolt of 1859. The fragment exemplified how thoughtful inclusions from the museum’s holdings complicated the exhibition’s material histories.

YEONSOON CHANG ’s

Worincheongang I-IV , 2025, abacá and indigo dyeing, 82 x 12.5 x 84.5 cm, at “Hyundai Translocal Series: Entangled and Woven,” the Whitworth, Manchester, 2026. Photo by Wooil Kim. Copyright the Cheongju Craft Biennale Organizing Committee. Courtesy the Whitworth.

SOMI KO ’s

People of One, Moment and Continuum , 2025 (left); and

PÉRO ’s

Entangled Memories, Interwoven Stories , 2025 (right), at “Hyundai Translocal Series: Entangled and Woven,” the Whitworth, Manchester, 2026. Photo by Michael Pollard. Courtesy the Whitworth.

Extending the theme of spiritual symmetries, Sumakshi Singh’s Spanning the Void (2025) recreates a bridge in Cheongju with delicate lace. The intricately worked gossamer threads replicate the bridge’s wooden texture and the swastika embedded in its fencing, the latter speaking to the spread of Buddhism from India to East Asia along the Silk Road. Another piece of religious architecture could be found in Jounghye Yoo’s installation. The diaphanous layers of fabric—bearing gold embroidered patterns and Ajrakh hand-block printed and resistance-dyed motifs—are cut to resemble the gate of Vishwanath Temple in Varanasi. Like Singh and Yoo, the fashion label Péro uses the language of textiles to reinterpret architectural forms around the human body. Entangled Memories, Interwoven Stories (2015–25) consists entirely of stitching normally used to close seams and raw edges in clothing, and recalls the lattice screens of Mughal palaces. Its elaborate threadwork resembles that of an ornately patterned Chikankari mat from the Whitworth’s collection. Again, the artifact sheds light on colonial histories. Developed during the Mughal era, white-on-white Chikankari embroidery declined under British rule as it was outcompeted by industrially manufactured textiles. It survived as a domestic art, passed between women who used it to make a meager living.

Installation view of YOUNG IN HONG ’s Sacred Empires , 2025 (left), and White Cranes in Snowfall , 2024 (right), at “Hyundai Translocal Series: Entangled and Woven,” the Whitworth, Manchester, 2026. Photo by Michael Pollard. Courtesy the Whitworth.

The crafts of working-class women came into focus in Young In Hong’s Sacred Empires (2025). The series of flags was made with the Kala Raksha collective in Kutch, where different styles of embroidery and mirrorwork are celebrated as distinctive markers of communities. Adorned with dainty circular mirrors and vibrant stitching, the patchwork banners represent animal colonies and their fluid territories, positing identity as both intrinsic and responsive.

Mirrorwork embroidery was seen in Somi Ko’s People of One, Moment (2025), too. Here the glimmering circles are arranged on five panels of cotton in the shapes of dancing figures. These moments of ecstasy reveal a truth: we contain reflections of one another and, as such, are each other’s greatest teachers.

Chloe Chu is an art writer and editor based in London.

Street photography through an Australian lens – in pictures

From a sleepy restaurant to a climbing leopard, the Australian Street Photography awards celebrate the best contemporary street photos taken by Australians. Twenty-five finalists have been selected by an independent jury through Aussie Street, a platform for photographers.

The pictures celebrate ordinary public life through images of observation, chance, humour, tension, ambiguity and human connection. The exhibition is running in Sydney from November

Food Coma

The Great Escape

Into The Light

article_text:
In recent years, interest in fan fiction has risen right alongside Hollywood’s persistent investment in adapting pre-existing IP. Novels and plays in the book-to-screen pipeline are now simply another part of the ecosystem, and it seems fanfic as a viable IP isn’t just the latest trend, but an industry-wide move to appeal directly to pre-existing fanbases and trust narratives that have been tried and tested repeatedly.

Fanfic — the practice of fans writing fiction based on pre-existing work and characters, often with relationships that differ from the original canon — has grown so popular and expansive that it’s impossible to ignore. Contemporary fanfic is said to have originated in the late 1960s, when the “Star Trek” fandom wrote fanzines; a popular pairing was James T. Kirk and Spock.

Today, fanfic has moved online; one of the leading fanfic platforms, Archive of Our Own (AO3), hosts over 18 million works across more than 81,250 fandoms and averages over 125 million page views a day. While AO3’s readership continues to grow exponentially (November 2025 saw over 146.6 million weekly page views more than the previous November), fanfic is also breaking into mainstream culture, with people openly declaring themselves fanfic readers and even celebs weighing in on fanfic .

In world scope of cinema, the fanfic-to-mainstream film is still in its infancy. The first notable commercial hit was the 2015 erotic drama “ Fifty Shades of Grey .” Sam Taylor-Johnson adapted E. L. James’ 2011 eponymous novel, which originated as a “Twilight” alternate-universe fanfic, “Master of the Universe,” that reimagined Edward Cullen as a wealthy CEO who introduces Bella Swan to a world of BDSM.

“Fifty Shades of Grey” went on to make over $569 million at the box office, proving that its fanfic roots didn’t limit its commercial value. The film even spawned a three-film franchise, with the entire trilogy eventually pulling in over one billion dollars in box office bucks.

Just over a decade later, the latest major fanfic-originating production is “ The Love Hypothesis .” Claire Scanlon’s romance adapts Ali Hazelwood’s best-selling novel of the same name, in which PhD student Olive enters a fake-dating arrangement with young professor Adam, a plot that originated as “Star Wars” fan fiction, “Head Over Feet,” which plotted a romance between Rey Skywalker and Kylo Ren.

There’s also been Prime Video’s “ The Idea of You ,” based on a Harry Styles fanfic starring Anne Hathaway and Nicholas Galitzine; similarly, Netflix’s “After” series is based on novels by Anna Todd that began as Styles-inspired fanfic. The third season of “My Life with the Walter Boys” premiered this year, with a fourth on the horizon; the novel adapted for the series was a Wattpad original first.

And this year saw another fanfic breakthrough: the forthcoming “Alchemised,” once the second-most-read work on AO3 and now the subject of a history-making seven-figure pre-publication deal for the screen rights to SenLinYu’s novel. The dark fantasy book originated as a fanfic titled “Manacled,” reimagining “Harry Potter” characters Hermione Granger and Draco Malfoy in a romance embedded in a “The Handmaid’s Tale”-esque universe.

In all these productions, it’s not as simple as simply translating from page to screen; the adaptation process scrubs these works of any explicit references to the original fanfic subjects. Stripped of the original IP during book publication and again in screen adaptation, these works end up twice removed from their fanfic origins.

Here, the idea that Hollywood is truly interested in the creative possibilities of a fanfic-originating adaptation becomes weak. Instead, studios seem to be picking works that come with a hungry audience attached but can still exist independent of their roots. There can be very subtle nods to the original fanfic for dedicated fans but, on the whole, an audience member could view the film with no concept of its origin because it is so severed.

This is a new path for studios toward the same goal: a risk-averse choice likely to perform well because of its preexisting success.

Additionally, this new potential of fanfic-to-film productions should feel refreshing , bringing new voices to the forefront and stories that haven’t followed the traditional route to production. However, that veneer may not be as revolutionary as it first seems.

Looking at the stories making it to the big screen, you’ll see they are predominantly heterosexual romances. It’s an interesting observation when AO3 repeatedly reports that M/M relationships dominate its most popular ships, from Evan Buckley and Eddie Diaz of “ 9-1-1 ” to Ilya Rozonav and Shane Hollander of “ Heated Rivalry ” to Clark Kent and Bruce Wayne of “ Batman .”

And fanfic adaptations aren’t just capturing attention in the film industry; fanfic is also a promotional tool, with films that have nothing to do with fanfic embracing it.

For “ Wicker ,” a fanfic competition was launched in line with the film’s release: “Write a spicy story inspired by The Wicker Husband, the short story behind the film, for the chance to have it transformed into a fully produced Quinn Original.” It’s another example of fanfic’s mainstreaming in pop culture; it’s no longer confined to a shadowy corner of the internet, but is now a hunting ground for publishers and producers seeking new material.

It’s as if there’s a desire to tap into the hype of the fanfic moment without taking major risks. Fanfic making it to the big screen may not be the revolutionary breakthrough one might assume, but rather an extension of the remake-and-adaptation culture that has become the norm.

But what sticks is the potential of fanfic narratives, born of the desire to see resonant characters in new dynamics and situations. And Hollywood still hasn’t truly invested in that kind of originality.
excerpt_original: Fan fiction is so hot right now. At least, that’s what everyone says.

article_text:
Peter Nagy, the founder of Indian gallery Nature Morte, has died.

Born in Connecticut, Nagy had already established himself as an artist – known for his xerox works – when he and Alan Belcher founded the gallery in 1982 in New York’s East Village, their exhibitions reflecting Nagy’s studio interest in conceptualism.

The gallery closed in 1988, only to reopen almost a decade later when Nagy moved to New Delhi.

With artists including Bharti Kher, Jitash Khallat and Raqs Media Collective, Nature Morte grew to include a second New Delhi space and a gallery in Mumbai opened in January 2024, in the Dhanraj Mahal building.

Nagy’s own work is included in the collections of the Whitney Museum, the Los Angeles Museum of Contemporary Art, the Brooklyn Museum and the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

Nagy had been ill for some time and in a statement on social media, the gallery said: ‘Peter was clear that, when the time came, the gallery should not close its doors in mourning. To him, an exhibition was never about the gallery. It belonged to the artist who had poured themselves into it and to everyone who came to see it. He believed an artist’s moment should never be put on hold.’

ホーム > 作品情報 > 映画「トキシック・アベンジャー」

トキシック・アベンジャー

劇場公開日： 2026年11月13日

解説・あらすじ

数多くの低予算B級映画を世に送り出した映画製作会社トロマ・エンターテインメントの代表作として長年にわたりカルト的人気を誇る、1984年製作の映画「悪魔の毒々モンスター」をハリウッドでリブートしたホラーコメディ。有毒廃棄物によって醜悪な怪物と化した男が街のヒーローとなり巨大悪徳企業に立ち向かう姿を、容赦ないグロテスク描写とブラックユーモア満載で描く。 邪悪な巨大製薬企業BTHによる支配のもと、暴力と環境汚染に蝕まれた街セント・ロマ。亡き妻の連れ子と2人で暮らす気弱な清掃員ウィンストンは、BTHに雇われたギャングに襲われる。有毒廃棄物の水槽に投げ捨てられた彼は、醜い風貌で超人的なパワーをもつミュータント「トキシック・アベンジャー」として復活。街のならず者たちを一掃し地元のヒーローとなった彼は、諸悪の根源であるBTHのCEO・ボブとその一味との壮絶な戦いに身を投じていく。 テレビシリーズ「ゲーム・オブ・スローンズ」のピーター・ディンクレイジが主人公ウィンストンを演じ、ケビン・ベーコン、イライジャ・ウッド、ジェイコブ・トレンブレイ、テイラー・ペイジが共演。監督・脚本は「この世に私の居場所なんてない」のメイコン・ブレア。製作にはトロマ・エンターテインメントの創設者ロイド・カウフマンが名を連ねた。

article_text:
Andrew Garfield ’s portrayal of Sam Altman in “ Artificial ” is less than flattering, but there was a time when the actor deeply admired the OpenAI co-founder and CEO.

“The first time I saw Sam, he was testifying in front of Congress and he was saying incredibly righteous stuff,” Garfield said Monday night during a Q&A following an AMPAS screening of the film at the Academy Museum in Los Angeles. “He was talking about transparency; he was talking about the risks. He was very, very casually saying, ‘No, I don’t have any equity in OpenAI. I’m just doing this because I love the technology and I’m passionate and I actually care about human beings.’”

OpenAI was launched as a nonprofit before launching the ChatGPT app. The

Luca Guadagnino-directed “Artificial” chronicles the founding of OpenAI and the firing and quick rehiring of Altman.

“I thought it was also just incredibly courageous for an out gay tech genius to be sat in front of Republican congressmen who probably don’t believe in his right to exist,” Garfield said. “So all of these things were adding up for me, and I was in such deep admiration of him. I was like, ‘Oh, we need more of these.’ and then he was meditating with Jack Kornfield, who’s this incredible Buddhist teacher. I’m like, ‘This guy might be like my future best friend.’ I was like, ‘He’s genuinely great and he seems to really have his values and priorities in the right place.’”

Garfield stopped short of directly criticizing Altman. “He convinced me that he was nothing but purely altruistic, which, I mean, it’s all playing out. I’m not gonna comment on those things,” he said. “We all are seeing what’s happening and we can all have our own feelings and opinions of that.”

He added, “It’s terrifying … I feel like if enough artists and if enough people who have power can regulate, can be a part of a conversation of making sure that we aren’t just giving our future away, lose all of our autonomy, I think we’ll be maybe OK? I don’t know. I think that is about as hopeful as I can be.”

Garfield recently disputed Altman’s claim that the two men waved at each other when the movie was shooting in front of Altman’s San Francisco home.

Garfield was asked about Altman’s anecdote in a recent GQ interview, and he said he “wasn’t there.”

“No, I saw that interview and I replayed it a few times to try and discern what he was actually saying, because I was very confused by that. I never had any interaction with him,” said Garfield. “I’ve never seen him in real life. We were shooting outside of his house. It was an eerie day, for sure. We were told that he wasn’t home and his security people were there. I think I saw one security guard. But, no, I never saw Sam, so he maybe mistook someone else for me. I have no idea, but I’ve never waved at Sam. I’ve never seen him. I was curious about that.”

"Artificial" star Andrew Garfield admits he once believed OpenAI’s Sam Altman was "genuinely great" and that he could be "my future best friend." https://t.co/izCsfrgrXQ via @variety #justforvariety pic.twitter.com/1B4DDQZP4T — Marc Malkin (@marcmalkin) November 10, 2026

While Garfield didn’t reach out to Altman to prepare for the role, he told me in July that he wouldn’t mind meeting the tech exec . “I wouldn’t know how to. I don’t have his number. I don’t have his email,” Garfield said. “But I’m sure that he’d be able to reach me if he wants to. I’d be very excited and curious to talk with him if he would ever want to do that.”

article_text:
A nother year, another raunchy comedy-drama in which Alexander Skarsgård is the answer to a social outcast’s erotic dreams. “I fucking loved Pillion so much!” says Olivia Colman, reliably sweary straight out of the gate, as she brings up last year’s British indie hit starring Skarsgård as a leather-clad dom with a timid traffic warden as his submissive. “And when they kissed at the end … Aww .” The 52-year-old Oscar-winner for The Favourite gives a mock-sniffle and a little shake of her frizzy grey locks, then pretends to dab her eyes.

Seated beside her in a London hotel room and wearing a bright orange “I’m With Stupid” T-shirt, Skarsgård tilts his head appreciatively. In Pillion, it was Harry Melling who had the privilege of being ravaged by the 50-year-old Swedish actor. Now it is Colman’s turn in Wicker, an earthy adult fairytale filmed in Budapest and set in a medieval village populated almost exclusively by British comic actors who converse in language both archaically formal (“Happy to transact with you”) and bluntly colloquial (“I’d better fuck off”). Among them is Phil Daniels as a leering butcher and Richard E Grant as a doctor who is even more inept at his job than Grant was as a Celebrity Traitor.

Colman plays the Fisherwoman, ridiculed by the other villagers for her pong and her general absence of allure. In the spirit of mocking the dominant patriarchal conventions, where men put metal collars on their wives when they get married, she asks the Basketmaker (Peter Dinklage) to fashion her a husband. A month later, she has a groom made entirely of wicker and dedicated solely to her pleasure and happiness. If the movie works, says Alex Huston Fischer, who wrote and directed Wicker with his wife, Eleanor Wilson, “you are essentially connecting emotionally to a basket”.

This is where Skarsgård comes in. His performance as the Wicker Husband was augmented by Weta Workshop, the New Zealand special-effects outfit behind the Lord of the Rings series. “I had a full bodysuit, a mask glued to my face, then added prosthetics for lips and eyelashes,” the actor says. “Oh, and hair made from flax. Highly flammable.” He tried out different accents but that felt “too removed from myself, what with the mask and everything else”. Colman gives an amused snort: “Might as well have got someone else in,” she says. Her co-star responds by puffing out his chest: “Hey, people pay big bucks to see Alexander Skarsgård on screen!”

In truth, he is humbler than all that. “Alex gets very awkward with compliments,” says Colman, then turns to him: “Well, tough . I don’t think there are many people who could have got quite so much across while acting within such restrictions. It’s a mark of how good you are. Sorry!” Is it fair to call his performance minimalist? “From my point of view, it was maximalist,” he says. “Because of the mask, I had to exaggerate everything and it felt like I was being hammy. Subtleties wouldn’t register. Underneath that beautifully crafted suit, I was like: ‘Aaah!’, ‘Grrr!’” His guttural sounds are accompanied by facial expressions which suggest a beginner’s guide to semaphore acting.

Skarsgård’s performance and the cross-hatched weave effect are magically textured. The impact of the creaking sound design should not be underestimated either, especially once the newlyweds get down to conjugal business. As one Letterboxd user put it: “Whoever chose the erection sound effect … you’re a genius and I love you.”

It turns out I’m not the only one amused by Wicker’s Letterboxd reviews. “As a director, you should never read the comments,” says Fischer. “But these ones are so entertaining.” Users have offered alternative titles (John Wicker, The Shape of Wicker, Fifty Shades of Hay), double entendres (“All my eggs are going in his basket”) and the witty suggestion that Etsy could become the new Hinge. One astute comment likened Elizabeth Debicki’s character, a jealous neighbour who tries to sabotage the Fisherwoman’s happiness, to the spiteful Emma, played by Mercedes McCambridge, in the classic western Johnny Guitar.

In any discussion of Wicker, the word “horny” is never far away. “We even included it when we pitched the movie,” says Fischer. “There’s something so human about it,” says Wilson. “We are these fleshy bodies with desires that are embarrassing and messy. It seemed like a great place for comedy.” Fischer notes that Colman’s goggle-eyed reactions were vital: “For someone to be surprised by incredible sex is very funny to us. Especially when it’s Olivia. She’s so good.”

Colman returns the compliment. “You get sent a lot of scripts that you feel you’ve seen before. But when I read this, I was like an octopus. I changed colour and went: ‘Oooh!’” A deft impression of a cephalopod follows, arms undulating. The Fisherwoman is the only female character with her own name, Colman points out, rather than being known as, say, The Bakerwoman or The Innkeeper’s Wife. “And she’s the only woman with agency. She’s perfectly happy with her life. It’s when pushed that she says, ‘I’m going to fuck this up and make a mockery of your beloved convention of marriage.’ Then she gets this kind, beautiful creature, and suddenly the world is even more joyous.”

Wicker is based on Ursula Wills’ short story The Wicker Husband, which has already been adapted as a stage musical combining actors and puppetry. Reviewing that version in 2020 , the Guardian theatre critic Arifa Akbar saw it as a story about “insider parochialism, the demonising of outsiders and the tyranny of conformity” with “echoes of Brexit Britain”. All pertinent, the directors agree now. “Those things were in our heads when we were writing,” says Fischer. “Elizabeth’s character is trying to protect herself and the village from what she sees as this foreign element that is there to destroy them.”

Dev Patel was originally set to play Colman’s basket-case beau until a scheduling clash forced him to pull out. Never having quite shed his Slumdog Millionaire innocence, Patel seems a more natural choice for the part than Skarsgård, who even prior to Pillion was drawn to stone-cold alphas: a tech bro (Succession), a violent husband (Big Little Lies), a coke-snorting cop (War on Everyone). Even he admits that he is cast against type in Wicker. “I tend to play characters who are messed up or internally conflicted. That duality is something I’ve done a lot and still enjoy. That wasn’t there for this character: he has a purity to him that was different to what I’ve done in the past. It was about making him relatable and interesting without that inner struggle. So that was a bit of a departure, and slightly intimidating.” Wilson argues, though, that Skarsgård has “qualities that are very Wicker Husband: he has a stoicism, and such presence. We needed that. It’s the sweetness that is the big surprise.”

The Fisherwoman’s newfound fulfilment and her husband’s inherent goodness eventually have a destabilising effect on the other villagers, who realise how impoverished their own lives are by comparison. Trouble follows. Had the honeymoon period between the couple continued, however, would it not have got irritating eventually? Don’t relationships need a little creative friction to remain interesting? “Oh, I don’t know,” says Colman, thoroughly unconvinced. “I quite like a friction-free life. I don’t think I’d cope with a fighty relationship. I prefer to work things out gently.”

Her thoughts turn to her own marriage to writer and producer Ed Sinclair, with whom she has three children. “We’ve been together for 32 years and married for 25,” she says. They have also worked together several times, including on Wicker, which they co-produced. While their domestic life is harmonious, there have nevertheless been “moments with the odd little look” in a professional context. She gives an example of one such look. The narrowed eyes, the abrupt withdrawal of warmth: no one would want to be on the receiving end of that. All the cosy Olivia Colman-ness has drained away in an instant.

“But we’ve never had big fights,” she says, back in chirpy mode again. “Very early on, when we first started working together, there was a suggestion from him of an acting note.” Hearing this, Skarsgård lets out a wicked laugh, instantly spotting a taboo. “Strong side eye,” he says. She continues: “Or sometimes when I’ve needed to do a taped audition, I’d say: ‘Can you tape this for me?’ And he’d ask, ‘Have you thought of trying it like this … ?’” There’s that look again. “Then he’d say, ‘OK, point taken!’”

Where does she think Wicker ends up vis-a-vis marriage? “I’d say it’s pro equal relationships. It’s perfectly possible to do it nicely. If you’re planning to share your life with someone, be considerate. Ask yourself: Have I been a good partner this week?” She draws a tick in the air with her finger. “Check!”

article_text:
AI is continuing to be implemented in the post-production stages of studio films, though “Hunger Games” franchise producer Nina Jacobson still views it as a “tool for artists” and “not a substitute” for them.

During a conversation with IndieWire editor-in-chief Brent Lang at IndieWire’s Future of Filmmaking Summit in Los Angeles Jacobson said the team used AI approximations of actors to test out new line readings for the upcoming prequel “Sunrise on the Reaping.” Those lines would then be recorded with the cast in traditional automated dialogue replacement process.

“We just finished [post-production], fairly recently, on ‘Sunrise on the Reaping.’ We used [AI] very specifically as a tool — within production, within post-production — while, at the same time, never using it to ever replace any of our artists or anything you see onscreen,” Jacobson said. “When you have ADR you want try out, you used to either have the editor getting in there with the lines you wanted … Just for something you’re trying out that you might not even keep. [AI] is a great tool to use ADR.”

Jacobson went on to explain how the technology has relatively limited applications for her, none of which find their way onto the screen.

“They can duplicate a voice. You can have the thing that you want to go get, or do a slug that actually looks like what you want … But we would still never use it because it’s not our actors,” she continued. “We’d go to our writer for the dialogue. I don’t ask Claude, ‘What should they say?’ I don’t ask Claude to finish the movie for us. But as a tool within production [and] within post-production that advances your work, and ultimately gets you to a better creative outcome, it’s crazy not to make use of the tool that the entire world now seems to be hinging upon.”

The prequel “Sunrise on the Reaping,” in theaters from Lionsgate on November 20, is the sixth film adaptation of Suzanne Collins’ popular young adult books series. The movie franchise first launched in 2012, with three additional entries produced quickly in the immediate years. Lionsgate revived the property in 2023 with the prequel “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes,” exploring the early politicking of the dystopian world of Panem and how the tyrant President Snow came to power.

“We don’t make the movies unless [Collins] writes a book. We’re not trying to just milk this title,” Jacobson said when asked about the franchise’s longevity. “They speak so much to the way that we live now and how we are living. The last one was really about the allure of authoritarianism. Why do we embrace it as a political system? Why are people drawn to it? … This one is about resistance: the cost of [it, and] the fact that just because something is a certain way today does not mean it always will be. You cannot predict the future based on the status quo.”

“Young people are growing up at a time where it seems impossible that we would ever be able to address climate change or the recession in democracy that we’ve seen across the globe, and yet it is that propaganda that kind of keeps you in that place of believing there’s nothing I can do to make a difference,” Jacobson continued. “Sometimes you won’t see the consequences of your resistance [in] four years, or maybe even in your lifetime. But it still adds up. … Whether you’ve seen none of the movies or all of them, it feels very much like a movie about the times we live in.”

Along with Jacobson’s “Hunger Games” talk, the producer touched on other projects from her film production company Color Force, including the coming “Dirty Dancing” sequel starring Jennifer Grey and HBO’s “Crazy Rich Asians” series. IndieWire’s Future of Filmmaking Summit also included a keynote by directors Phil Lord and Chris Miller, diving into the production of their sci-fi blockbuster “Project Hail Mary,” and a one-on-one with Bill Hader on what he learned making his upcoming feature debut “They Know.”

Watch the complete conversation with Jacobson in the video above.

IndieWire Future of Filmmaking 2026 Summit is presented by AT&T Untold Stories, an impactful multi-year collaboration between AT&T and Tribeca Festival that awards $1.2 million dollars, mentorship, and comprehensive support to the next generation of filmmakers looking to bring their films to the big screen. For more information, visit here .

article_text:
O nce a year, Corvo, the smallest and most northerly island of Portugal’s Azores archipelago, goes dark. Since 2019, the island’s 450 or so inhabitants have chosen to switch off the lights every autumn for five nights to tackle the disastrous effects of artificial light on Cory’s shearwaters, a seabird endemic to the Atlantic Ocean.

It began in 1991 when the community noticed huge numbers of deaths among young shearwaters.

The juveniles spend three months in their nests before attempting their first flight to the ocean, orienting themselves by the stars.

Unfortunately, many are fatally confused by the artificial glow of streetlights, and end up crashing into Vila do Corvo’s narrow streets.

Local people began rescuing them at night, roaming through the village in the dark. This inspired other communities, and in 1995, the Azorean government launched the “ SOS Cagarro ” [shearwaters] campaign to include the other eight islands.

In subsequent years, the Portuguese Society for the Study of Birds (SPEA) joined the project, helping it grow.

I discovered the initiative on my second trip to Corvo, in June 2024. I knew of the Cory’s shearwater because I had travelled to the Azores before and had the chance to observe them in the open sea.

But it was not until I saw a campaign sticker in a shop on the island that I found out about the blackout. When it was explained to me, I decided to come back and document it.

To me, the message of this story is that there is always hope, especially when we involve future generations and teach them to care about our planet and its beauty.

Today, Corvo is still the only island that performs a full blackout of public illumination to help the birds find their way to the ocean without interference from artificial lights.

The island sinks into darkness and the stars can be seen clearly; the birds begin their journeys, hoping to find their way to the ocean, while people walk through Vila do Corvo, the only village on the island, to find and rescue any fallen birds.

Those rescued will be placed in cardboard boxes overnight to recover, and released the next day from a cliff close to the ocean, giving them a second chance to reach the water, their new home.

The campaign says more than 30,000 Cory’s shearwater fledglings have been rescued in the Azores since 2015 – about 6,000 of them on Corvo alone.

This collective effort is a powerful example of how reducing light pollution can restore ecological balance . It demonstrates that small changes can significantly affect biodiversity.

How can an action like this inspire global reflection? This intentional blackout is not just an act of conservation but a step towards developing the ability to coexist with nature without disrupting its rhythms.

Find more age of extinction coverage here , and follow the biodiversity reporters Rebecca Ratcliffe , Phoebe Weston and Patrick Greenfield in the Guardian app for more nature coverage.

人気を後押ししたと考えられるのが、英BBCのドラマ「Detectorists」だ。田園地帯で金属探知を楽しむ中年男性2人の友情と日常を描いた穏やかなコメディで、2014年から2017年にかけて全3シーズンが放送され、2022年には特別編も制作された。その影響もあってか、全英金属探知協議会（National Council for Metal Detecting）の会員数は、過去10年間で4倍になったと報じられている。

トラック運転手が畑で発見、古代ローマの金の指輪が博物館へ──発見者は住宅ローン完済｜イングランド南西部サマセット州の農地で金属探知機愛好家が発見したローマ時代の金の指輪が、地元の遺産保護団体に購入され、サマセット博物館で展示されることになった。【続きを読む】Photo: Courtesy South West Heritage Trust

イルミンスター近郊の農地で見つかったイルミンスター・リング。Photo: Courtesy South West Heritage Trust

英金属探知機愛好家、有機農場で古代ローマの鉛インゴットを発見。帝国時代の鉱物供給網のヒントに｜イギリス・ウェールズのセレディギオン州で、金属探知機愛好家の2人が古代ローマ時代の鉛インゴット2点を発見した。皇帝ドミティアヌスの刻印が残るこれらの遺物は、この地域がローマ帝国の資源供給網に組み込まれていたことを物語る貴重な証拠と考えられている。【続きを読む】 Photo: The Metal Detectives Group

金属探知機により発見された古代ローマの鉛インゴット。Photo: The Metal Detectives Group

（写真左から）ニック・ヤロープとピーター・ニコラス、土地所有者のジェライント・ジェンキンス。Photo: The Metal Detectives Group

金属探知機愛好家が「思わぬ場所」で金とガーネットの宝飾品を発見！｜2023年、イギリス東部リンカンシャー州ドニントン・オン・ベイン近郊の丘の斜面で、金属探知機愛好家が金とガーネットで作られたペンダントとブローチ計5点を発見した。この宝飾品群に関する調査結果が、このほど学術誌で発表された。【続きを読む】 Photo: The Portable Antiquities Scheme

盗難を恐れ3日間車中泊！ 金属探知機愛好家、6時間かけてローマ時代の硬貨1万5000枚を発掘｜北ウェールズで金属探知機愛好家が地中からローマ時代の硬貨1万5000枚が入った壺を探し当てた。イギリスで発見されたローマ硬貨の中では、2010年に見つかった5万2500枚に次ぐ規模となる。【続きを読む】 Photo: Facebook/Minelab Metal Detectors

金属探知機愛好家親子が畑で大発見。「子どものおもちゃ」と思った金属片が古代ローマのブローチだった！｜イギリス南部、ドーセット州ドーチェスターの畑で金属探知機愛好家親子が2000年前の青銅製ブローチを発見した。ブローチは現在、宝物認定の調査が行われている。【続きを読む】Photo: BBC Spotlight

古代ローマのブローチを見つけたマーティン・ターナー。Photo: BBC Spotlight

金属探知機愛好家が「歴史の空白」を掘り起こす！ 模造金貨のジュエリーは権力の象徴？｜イギリス・エセックス州サクステッドで金蔵探知機愛好家が中世初期のものと思われる金製のペンダントヘッドを発見した。研究者は、ローマ帝国崩壊後の同州における支配階級の存在に新たな光を投げかけるものと注目している。【続きを読む】Photo: Courtesy Colchester and Ipswich Museum Services

金属探知機愛好家が見つけた、中世初期のものと思われる金貨ペンダント。Photo: Courtesy Colchester and Ipswich Museum Services

8歳の少年が19世紀の難破船を発見！｜家族旅行中の8歳の男の子が誕生日プレゼントにもらった金属探知機を使ってみたところ難破船をカナダ・オンタリオ州で発見した。「湖畔で金属探知機を起動すると、『チン！』という音がし、掘ってみると大きな釘が出てきたのです」と、男の子は当時を振り返る【続きを読む】Photo: YouTube/CBC News: The National

金属探知機愛好家が申告不履行などの罪で逮捕｜イギリスで金属探知機愛好家によって発見された933枚の鉄器時代の金貨が発見された。発見者は財宝申告の不履行と窃盗の罪で逮捕された。申告を怠った発見者には報奨金が支給されず、土地の所有者のみに支払われた。なお、金貨は地元の博物館に収蔵されている。【続きを読む】Photo: Facebook/Museum of Chelmsford

畑から1400年前の純金製カラスの頭部が出土！｜金属探知機愛好家グループの新人を含む2人が2025年1月、アングロサクソン時代の金製のカラスの頭部とガーネットが埋め込まれた帯を発掘した。神話では使徒や身の前触れとして登場していたカラスだが、今回見つかった頭部が何を表現しているかはわかっていない【続きを読む】Photo: Chris Phillips

浜辺を散歩中の金属探知機愛好家が「真の芸術品」を発見！｜ポーランド・ポメラニアで、嵐の後の浜辺を探索した金属探知機愛好家が2500年前の短剣を発見。刃の根元に星に囲まれた小さな三日月のようなシンボルが、全体には星を線で繋いだ星座のような形が施されており、儀式的意義をもっていたと推測している。【続きを読む】Photo: Museum of the History of the Kamień Region

短剣の根元の拡大図。Photo: Museum of the History of the Kamień Region

イギリスで鉄器時代のお宝800点超を発見。馬具に地中海サンゴの装飾など古代史に新たな光｜イギリスのノース・ヨークシャー州メルソンビー近郊の畑で、800点を超える鉄器時代の遺物が見つかった。この種の発見としては最大規模かつ重要性が高く、イングランド北部と古代ローマの交易を示す遺物も出土している。【続きを読む】Photo: Courtesy Durham University

title_original: Lorna Simpson Wins $105,000 Wolfgang Hahn Prize
editorial_title_zh: 洛娜·辛普森荣获105,000美元沃尔夫冈·哈恩奖
editorial_excerpt_zh: 该奖项用于支持科隆路德维希博物馆对艺术品进行收藏。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "开创概念摄影新方法的美国艺术家洛娜·辛普森（Lorna Simpson）被评为2027年沃尔夫冈·哈恩奖（Wolfgang Hahn Prize）的得主。赞助该年度奖项的德国科隆路德维希博物馆（Museum Ludwig）将出资100,000欧元（约合105,000美元）用于为馆藏收购一件辛普森的作品。该机构将于明年为她举办一场个人展览，并配合出版物发行。", "links": [{"text": "Wolfgang Hahn Prize", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/t/wolfgang-hahn-prize/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2027年奖项评审团由纽约古根海姆博物馆副馆长兼首席策展人、第16届卡塞尔文献展艺术总监娜奥米·贝克维斯（Naomi Beckwith）以及路德维希博物馆董事会组成。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "辛普森出生于布鲁克林，在1990年代凭借将图像与碎片化文字相结合的多层照片在国际上崭露头角。她的创作实践最终扩展到电影、绘画、素描和雕塑，常常模糊媒介之间的界限，同时始终关注黑人女性的内心世界和大众认知。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她由两部分组成的图文作品《ID》（1990）曾入选路德维希博物馆1999年的群展“艺术世界的对话（Kunstwelten im Dialog）”。在该作品中，辛普森将黑人女性的两幅肖像并置。在一幅中，她背对镜头；一幅刻有“身份”（identity）一词的牌匾安装在图像旁。另一幅仅露出她的头顶，酷似从深空浮现的地球。一块刻有“辨认”（identify）一词的牌匾安装在该图像上方。该博物馆1999年的目录文本将《ID》与科隆黑麦当娜进行了比较，后者是一尊著名的木质雕像，也是该机构附近一座17世纪教堂内的朝圣地。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "博物馆在一份声明中表示：“在评审团看来，她那多面性的作品将为路德维希博物馆的美国艺术收藏提供重要的推动力。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "声明接着指出，此次收购“将进一步发展波普艺术及其对受媒体影响的意象之运用的立场，彼得和艾琳·路德维希（Peter and Irene Ludwig）早期对此进行了相当深度的收藏”。博物馆将辛普森的作品描述为通往戴安娜·斯蒂格利（Diamond Stingily）和卡罗琳·拉扎德（Carolyn Lazard）创作实践的“桥梁”，后两者的作品通过“青年收购”（Junger Ankauf）计划新近进入该馆收藏，并“反思了非裔美国女性的自我形象”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "沃尔夫冈·哈恩奖设立于1994年，旨在表彰那些拥有国际认可的创作成果、但在德国尚未广为人知的成熟当代艺术家。往届得主包括李禹焕、弗朗西斯·阿利斯（Francis Alÿs）、克里·詹姆斯·马歇尔（Kerry James Marshall）、贝蒂·萨尔（Betye Saar）、弗兰克·鲍林（Frank Bowling）和梁慧圭（Haegue Yang）等人。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
American artist Lorna Simpson, who pioneered a new approach to conceptual photography, has been named the winner of the 2027 Wolfgang Hahn Prize . The Museum Ludwig in Cologne, Germany, which sponsors the annual prize, will put €100,000 (about $105,000) toward the acquisition of a work by Simpson for its collection. A solo exhibition of her work will staged by the institution next year, accompanied by a publication.

The 2027 award jury comprised Naomi Beckwith, deputy director and chief curator of the Guggenheim Museum in New York, and artistic director of documenta 16, and the Museum Ludwig board.

Born in Brooklyn, Simpson rose to international renown in the 1990s with multilayered photographs that pair images with fragmented text. Her practice eventually expanded to encompass film, painting, drawing, and sculpture, often blending the boundaries between mediums while remaining focused on inner worlds and popular perceptions of Black women.

Her two-part photo-text work ID (1990) was included in Museum Ludwig’s 1999 group exhibition “Art Worlds in Dialogue (Kunstwelten im Dialog).” In that work, Simpson paired two portraits of a Black woman. In one, she turns her back to the camera; a plaque bearing the word “identity” is mounted alongside the image. The other reveals only the crown of her head, which resembles the Earth emerging from deep space. A plaque engraved with the word “identify” is mounted over this image. The museum’s catalog text from 1999 compared ID to the Black Madonna of Cologne, a famous wooden statute and site of pilgrimage housed in a 17th-century church near the institution.

“Her multifaceted body of work will provide, in the jury’s view, an important impetus for the Museum Ludwig’s collection of American art,” the museum said in a statement.

The statement continued that the acquisition “will further develop the positions in Pop Art and its use of media-influenced imagery, which Peter and Irene Ludwig acquired early on and in considerable depth.” The museum described Simpson’s work as “a bridge” to the practices of Diamond Stingily and Carolyn Lazard, whose works newly entered its collection through the Junger Ankauf initiative and “reflect on the self-image of African American women.”

Established in 1994, the Wolfgang Hahn Prize honors established contemporary artists with internationally recognized bodies of work who are not yet widely known in Germany. Previous recipients include Lee Ufan, Francis Alÿs, Kerry James Marshall, Betye Saar, Frank Bowling, and Haegue Yang.

Black Church Bay

In a sleepy Welsh fishing village, Barry’s life starts to unravel after an intimate encounter in this gripping mystery drama starring Tom Cullen and Joe Locke.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Rhys Marc Jones

With Tom Cullen, Joe Locke, Marli Siu

UK 2026. 107min

Courtesy of Vertigo Releasing Ltd

Language English

Access information

Thursday 15 October 18:30

Audio description

Audio description

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Barry has always kept his personal life tightly under wraps. But as hidden truths come to light, he is no longer able to control the double life he leads. Barry must decide what lengths he will go to cover up his private life and ultimately his true self. Black Church Bay is a tense and thought-provoking drama that affirms Rhys Marc Jones as an exciting queer filmmaker.

Grace Barber-Plentie

Content advice

Contains scenes of nudity and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Moonglow

A Long Winter

Andrew Haigh’s sensitive drama transforms a snowbound landscape into a space where beauty and longing exist in delicate equilibrium.

Frank and Percy

Roger Allam and Ian McKellen excel as the titular characters in this adaptation of the West End hit, about finding connection beyond your sixties.

title_original: 【レポート】「第78回 正倉院展」奈良国立博物館で11月9日まで　奈良時代の驚異のデザイン力と技術力に注目　科学調査で判明した雨を降らせるミイラ「虹龍」の謎の秘密も
editorial_title_zh: 【报道】“第78回 正仓院展”奈良国立博物馆开展至11月9日 聚焦奈良时代的惊异设计力与技术力 科学调查揭示能呼风唤雨的木乃伊“虹龙”的神秘面纱
editorial_excerpt_zh: 正如奈良国立博物馆馆长井上洋一所说：“在世界范围内，能以相同主题持续举办如此长时间的展览极其罕见。”已然成为奈良秋季传统活动、散发独特存在感的“第78回 正仓院展”于今日10月24日再度开幕，
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OCT01a-shousouinntenn-e1793084209428.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "北仓 漆胡瓶", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "正如奈良国立博物馆馆长井上洋一所说：“在世界范围内，能以相同主题持续举办如此长时间的展览极其罕见。”已然成为奈良秋季传统活动、散发独特存在感的“第78回 正仓院展”于今日10月24日再度开幕（展期至11月9日，期间无休）。虽然每年举办，但正仓院展的魅力在于每年展出的宝物各不相同（共计60件，其中11件为首次展出）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OCT02b-shousouinntenn.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "南仓 鸟兽花背方镜", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OCT03c-shousouinntenn.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "展板照片。设计有动作逼真、筋骨隆起的灵兽——狻猊", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "今年，让我们一同聚焦奈良时代令人惊叹的设计力与高超技术力，以及经科学调查弄清的、拥有呼风唤雨传说的神秘木乃伊“虹龙”的秘密，还有圣武天皇深为皈依的佛教戒律经典（《梵网经》）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "正仓院宝物是流传自东大寺正仓院正仓、在敕封管理下历经约1300年以奇迹般的保存状态流传至今的传世品群（约9000件）。圣武天皇逝世后，其夫人光明皇后将天皇的遗爱品献给东大寺的卢舍那佛（大佛），由此拉开序幕。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因此，展厅中最具视觉冲击力的展品当属超长的经卷《梵网经》（全卷展出）。这是流传至正仓院的代表性经卷，以卢舍那佛为主教，阐述了立志觉悟之人（菩萨）的心态等。应圣武天皇之邀将戒律传至日本的鉴真和尚东渡后，该经卷的书写盛极一时。可以说这是支撑圣武天皇笃诚信仰的基础，在某种意义上构成了正仓院宝物的核心。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OCT04-shousouinntenn.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "中仓 《梵网经》（局部）", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "作为主视觉海报的两个胡瓶——“漆胡瓶”与“白瑠璃瓶”同样不容错过。为此，我们向该展负责人、主任研究员三本周作请教了收录在圣武天皇遗爱品清单《国家珍宝帐》中的波斯风格水壶“漆胡瓶”的魅力所在。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "点缀展览开篇与结尾的“2个胡瓶”所展现的对比美", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OCT05e-shousouinntenn.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "北仓 漆胡瓶", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“漆胡瓶”是将长颈、鸟首壶嘴、弓形把手的波斯风格水壶以东亚漆艺技术打造而成，是象征丝绸之路东西方交流的宝物。其采用平脱技法，在黑漆地上贴上鹿、鸳鸯、花草等纹样的银薄片，然后剥除银片上的漆；同时采用卷胎技法，将薄木片卷起或层层叠垒制作而成。三本表示，工匠高超技术所支撑的“卓越设计感”以及“轮廓与纹样布局的方式”是其魅力所在。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "原本波斯胡瓶多呈“白瑠璃瓶”那般下部膨大的造型，而“漆胡瓶”通过卷胎技法拥有了圆润优美的球体壶身、纵长的壶颈与底足，“各部位比例极佳，具有独特且洗练的美丽轮廓，”三本说道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OCT06f-shousouinntenn.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "展板照片，展开图局部", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此外，谈到纹样时他解释道：“并非杂乱无章，而是具有规律性，从展开图可以看出，以中间为山峰呈对称布局。能在富有立体感的器物上进行如此张弛有度的设计，需要非凡的技术力和几何感性。”仔细观察纹样，小鹿斑纹乃至鸟类的细微羽毛都通过线刻表现出来，自然界的精准捕捉与重现所展现的高超雕金技术令人惊叹。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OCT07g-shousouinntenn.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "中仓 白瑠璃瓶", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "另一方面，在设计上走简洁、对比路线的是采用碱石灰玻璃制作的“白瑠璃瓶”。为了方便断水，壶嘴边缘内卷，为了易于倾倒，把手并非笔直而是带有微妙的弧度，这是一件兼具功能美的胡瓶，请务必前往现场对比欣赏。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "令人眼花缭乱的惊异设计", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OCT08h-shousouinntenn.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "北仓 雕石横笛", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "与圣武天皇颇有渊源的石质横笛“雕石横笛”采用蛇纹岩模仿带有竹节的竹管，其上精细雕刻着正仓院纹样中常见的衔花鸟等设计。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OCT09i-shousouinntenn.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "中仓 密陀彩绘箱", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此外，在天平胜宝4年（752年）东大寺“大佛开眼会”上用于盛放2种香料并献上的供物箱“密陀彩绘箱”则采用了绘制喷火怪鸟的独特设计。箱身涂有掺入起清漆作用的密陀僧的油。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "究竟为何会成为宝物？能呼风唤雨的神奇之龙与首次展出的木乃伊化兽足之谜", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OCT10j-shousouinntenn.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "南仓 虹龙", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "您是否知道，正仓院藏有一件传说中在宝库开检时会带来降雨的异形宝物（木乃伊）？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "室町时代，它曾作为“龙日干”被记录：第6代将军足利义教在切取“兰奢待”的那天曾目睹过它，并记录说那天也下了雨；到了江户时代左右，它被称为“虹龙”。它的真实身份究竟是什么……", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "近年来，宫内厅正仓院事务所实施的动物来源素材宝物调查（牙甲角调查）表明，它大约是900年前的雌性日本鼬木乃伊。此外，木乃伊化的动物足部“兽足”作为宝物被收藏，经该调查确认为日本鬣羚或赤狐、亦或是其近缘物种，并在本次展览中首次展出。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OCT11jK-shousouinntenn.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "南仓 兽足 其1", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "关于“虹龙”，人们做出了各种推测：它是误入正仓院正仓后直接变成了木乃伊？还是祈雨或防火的咒术具……？至今仍是一个谜团重重的宝物。今年自开幕首日起就为奈良带来大雨的“虹龙”，是正仓院中即便科技进步也无法解开某种“未知”的神秘宝物之一。（撰稿人：泉由香）", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": article_text:
「これだけ長きにわたり、同じテーマで続いている展覧会は、世界的に見ても非常に珍しい」と奈良国立博物館の井上洋一館長が語るほど、もはや奈良の秋の伝統行事と言える存在感を放つ「第78回 正倉院展」が今年も10月24日に開幕しました（11月9日まで会期中無休）。 毎年開催でありつつも、お目にかかれる宝物は毎年違うのが正倉院展の魅力です（全60件、うち初出陳11件）。

今年は、奈良時代の驚くべきデザイン力と高い技術力、そして、科学調査で明らかになった雨を降らせる伝説を持つ謎のミイラ「 虹龍 」の秘密、聖武天皇が深く帰依した仏教の戒律を説いたお経（ 梵網経 ）に注目して見てみましょう。

正倉院宝物は、東大寺の正倉院正倉に伝来し、勅封管理で約1300年にわたり、奇跡的な保存状態で守り伝えられてきた伝世品群（約9000件）。聖武天皇の没後、妻の光明皇后により、天皇の遺愛品が東大寺の 盧舎那仏 （大仏）に献納されたことに始まります。

そのため、会場内で特にインパクトがあった展示は、非常に長いお経「梵網経」でした（一巻全展示）。正倉院に伝来する代表的な経巻で、盧舎那仏を教主として、悟りを目指す人（菩薩）の心のあり方などを説いたものです。聖武天皇の招きに応じて、日本へ戒律を伝えた鑑真和上の来朝以降にこの書写が盛んになりました。聖武天皇の篤い信仰心を支える基盤と言え、ある意味、正倉院宝物の根幹を成す品です。

メインビジュアルを飾った二つの 胡瓶 、「 漆胡瓶 」と「 白瑠璃瓶 」も見逃せません。そのうち、同展担当の三本周作主任研究員に聖武天皇の遺愛品リスト『 国家珍宝帳 』に記載されているペルシア風の水差し「漆胡瓶」の魅力を教えていただきました。

展示の最初と最後を彩る“２つの胡瓶”の対照的な美

「漆胡瓶」は、長い首、鳥の頭をかたどった注口、弓なりの 把手 が付くペルシア風の水差しを東アジアの漆工技術でつくり上げた、シルクロードの東西交流を象徴する宝物。黒漆地にシカやオシドリ、草花といった文様の銀の薄板を貼り、銀板の上の漆だけを剥ぎ取った 平脱 技法、木の薄板を巻き上げ、もしくは輪積みした 巻胎 技法でつくられています。三本さんは、工人の高度な技術力に裏打ちされた「優れたデザインセンス」と「シルエットと文様の配置の仕方」が魅力だと語ります。

もともとペルシアの胡瓶は、「白瑠璃瓶」のように下膨れの形が多いのですが、「漆胡瓶」は、巻胎によって、丸っとした美しい球体のシルエットの胴、縦長の首と足を持ち、「各部のバランスが優れており、独自の洗練された美しいシルエットが特徴です」と三本さん。

さらに文様についても「無秩序ではなく、規則性があり、展開図を見ると、真ん中を山として対称的に配置されているのが分かります。メリハリがある立体器物にこのようにデザインできるのは、すごい技術力と幾何のセンスが必要です」と説明します。文様をよく見ると、鹿の子模様や鳥の細かな毛まで線彫りで表現され、自然界を正確に捉え、再現する彫金技術の高さに驚かされます。

一方で、デザインとしてはシンプルで対照的なのが、アルカリ石灰ガラスでつくられた「白瑠璃瓶」です。水切りをよくするため、注口の縁の部分が内側に丸みがあることや、注ぎやすくするため、把手が真っ直ぐではなく微妙に曲がっているといった機能美に長けた胡瓶なので、ぜひ見比べてみましょう。

めくるめく驚異のデザイン

聖武天皇ゆかりの石製の横笛「 彫石横笛 」は、蛇紋岩で節を持つ竹管をかたどっており、正倉院文様でお馴染みの花喰鳥などが細かく彫られたデザインです。

他にも、天平勝宝4年（752年）の東大寺「 大仏開眼会 」で、２種類のお香を入れて献納された献物箱「 密陀彩絵箱 」は、火を噴く怪鳥が描かれたユニークなデザイン。ニスの役割を持つ 密陀僧 をまぜた油が塗布されています。

一体なぜ宝物に？雨を降らせる不思議な龍と初出陳のミイラ化した獣足の謎

正倉院には、宝庫の開検時に雨を降らせる龍（ミイラ）だと伝わる異形の宝物があるのをご存じでしょうか？

室町時代には、「 龍日干 」として、6代将軍・足利義教が「 蘭奢待 」を切り取った日に目撃し、その日も雨が降ったと記録されており、江戸時代頃に「 虹龍 」と呼ばれるようになりました。一体、正体は何なのか…

近年、宮内庁正倉院事務所が行った動物由来素材の宝物調査（牙甲角調査）により、約900年前のメスのニホンテンのミイラだと判明。他にも、ミイラ化した動物の脚「獣足」が宝物として納められており、同調査でニホンカモシカとアカギツネ、もしくはその類縁種だと判明し、今回初出陳されています。

「虹龍」は、正倉院正倉に迷い込んで、そのままミイラ化したのでは？とも、雨乞いや火災除けの呪術具だったのでは…？とも、様々な想定がなされているいまだ謎多き宝物。今年も開幕初日から、奈良に大雨を降らせた「虹龍」は、科学が進んでも解明できない“何か”を持っている正倉院のミステリアスな宝物のひとつです。（ライター・いずみゆか）

正倉院展のチケットは美術展ナビチケットアプリ（スマホ）で好評発売中

Contents

1 Going out: Cinema

2 Going out: Gigs

3 Going out: Art

4 Going out: Stage

5 Staying in: Streaming

6 Staying in: Games

7 Staying in: Albums

8 Staying in: Brain food

Going out: Cinema

Wildwood Out now If Pixar was a chocolate bar, it would be a Mars, while Laika – whose new film Wildwood incorporates themes of war and child abduction – would be something like Green & Blacks. Darker and with more esoteric flavours, this stop-motion animation is not so much for the nursery school crowd, but for discerning pre-teens and adults alike. Ghosts: The Possession of Button House Out now The beloved BBC TV comedy gets a big-screen outing, with Simon Farnaby’s trouserless Tory MP ghost, Jim Howick’s dead scoutmaster, shot by a member of his own troop, Ben Willbond’s closeted second world war officer and the other regular cast members all returning. Fatherland Out now Joint winner of the best director prize at Cannes, Paweł Pawlikowski’s latest is set during the cold war, and sees an actor, writer and rally driver, Erika (Sandra Hüller), set off on a road trip across Germany with her dear old dad, the Nobel prize-winning writer Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler). Ali G: Who Iz I? Out now Twenty four years after Ali G Indahouse opened at No 1 at the UK box office, Sasha Baron Cohen revives his alter-ego for a followup, making his directorial debut in the process. Morgana Robinson also stars. Catherine Bray

Going out: Gigs

Suede, Manic Street Preachers OVO Hydro, Glasgow, 28 October; First Direct Bank Arena Leeds, 30 October; touring to 12 November Christmas comes early for people of a certain vintage with a penchant for evergreen British rock bands in the shape of this co-headline tour. Expect a smattering of newer material – Antidepressants, the most recent opus by Suede is Mercury-nominated – and some undeniable classics from both. Michael Cragg

Jasmine Myra Norwich Arts Centre, 27 October; Earth, London, 28 October; St George’s, Bristol, 29 October Alto saxophonist-composer Jasmine Myra is on the rise within the cinematic spiritual jazz orbit of Manchester’s Gondwana Records, a visionary operation devoted to the soulful lyricism and storytelling she espouses. This tour will be a fascinating insight into just how far the very promising Myra is instrumentally ready to go. John Fordham

False Idols Halloween Drumsheds, London, 24 October Queer club night False Idols returns to London for a special Halloween blowout featuring Boo! Bitch! hitmaker Kim Petras. Other spooky banger merchants on the bill include Swedish alt-popper Cobrah, London’s Rose Gray and US rapper Cakes da Killa. MC

London Symphony Orchestra/Pappano Barbican Hall, London, 29 October The LSO is the latest major international institution to commission British composer Hannah Kendall, a distinctive, ambitious voice in contemporary classical music. Her new work I Have Discovered the Secret of Death features Grammy-winning mezzo Fleur Barron. Its world premiere is paired with Tchaikovsky’s impassioned Fifth Symphony. Antonio Pappano conducts. Flora Willson

Going out: Art

Wilhelmina Barns-Graham Tate St Ives, to 3 May A big part of St Ives’s modernist boom in the early 2oth century, Barns-Graham (work pictured above) quietly became one of the UK’s most important artists of her era with an emotional take on abstraction, celebrated here with 170 works from throughout her career.

LS Lowry MK Gallery, Milton Keynes, to 28 February This big celebration of the life and work of one of England’s best-loved artists is the first institutional show of his grimy, gritty industrial painting for 13 years, and marks 50 years since his death.

The Rupture: No Condition Is Permanent Talbot Rice Gallery, Edinburgh, to 13 February Attempting to respond to a time of unprecedented political, social and economic change, this exhibition brings together a huge cast of international artists to reckon with our increasingly broken systems.

The Way We Live The Box, Plymouth, to 21 February This exhibition looks at the idea of the home, and what it means to a variety of artists including the likes of Do Ho Suh, Rachel Whiteread and recent Turner prize winner Jasleen Kaur. Eddy Frankel

Going out: Stage

The Lives of Others Adelphi theatre, London, to 9 January Director Robert Icke adapts the Academy award-winning film set in East Berlin, 1984. A writer and an actor are put under state surveillance – and a Stasi operative is inexorably drawn into their lives. Keira Knightley, Stephen Dillane and Luke Thompson star. Miriam Gillinson

Macbeth Liquid & Envy, Oldham, to 7 November While Oldham’s Coliseum theatre is being restored, it is staging work in imaginative locations around town. This site-specific take on Macbeth is set in a real-life nightclub, invoking a world of 70s gangsters, casinos and shifting social codes. MG

Hansel & Gretel and the Witch Northern Stage, Newcastle upon Tyne, 29 October to 1 November Choreographer Liv Lorent and her company BalletLorent have really cornered the market in fairytale family shows with a bit of edge and a lot of imagination. The latest is a new take on Hansel & Gretel that promises a brand new ending courtesy of its writer, the former poet laureate Carol Ann Duffy. Lyndsey Winship

Susan Calman Touring to 20 November The Glaswegian standup has presented a slew of TV programmes and done a Strictly shift in the decade since her last tour, but new show Tall Tales – which combines showbiz stories with meditations on grief and depression – proves this glam career pivot has done nothing to dent her twinkly misanthropy. Rachel Aroesti

after newsletter promotion

Staying in: Streaming

Nocturne Apple TV, 30 October Stephen Graham is back in his most sinister role yet: a serial killer who is apparently able to murder from the confines of his underground cell. This psychological thriller (above) pits him against not one but two haunted detectives: Liev Schreiber’s ex-soldier Jonah and his protege Saga (Zazie Beetz).

A Course Called Ireland iPlayer & BBC Two, 25 October, 9.30pm As a genre, the celebrity travelogue has become tired and bloated, but this new series is fuelled by an unusual level of star power, as the one and only Bill Murrray embarks on a golf-based trip around Ireland. Extra craic comes courtesy of guests including Chris O’Dowd and Joanne McNally.

Minimum Wage Netflix, 25 October What started out as a micro-budget webseries about incompetent teens manning a pizzeria has been turned into a 28-part sitcom by Netflix, who will be hoping its cast – including newly recruited SNL cast member Grace Reiter – become comedy’s next big things.

Beat Luke Littler Netflix, 30 October Is darts really that hard? Find out this Friday, as 20 amateurs take on the 19-year-old world No 1 in Manchester in an attempt to win £501,000. The event will be streamed live, with Gary Lineker on hosting duties and Richard Osman contributing Pointless-style statistics. RA

Staying in: Games

Pardon My French Toast PC, Switch 2, out 29 October A brightly coloured 3D platformer, in which you’re a slice of anthropomorphic brioche toast able to cover himself in different spreads to gain a range of special abilities. Like a ZX Spectrum classic reheated for the 21st century.

Phantom Blade Zero PC, PS5, out 29 October An elite assassin is framed for murder and must prove his innocence while a fatal wound slowly kills him. Stylised martial arts in a dark fantasy realm? Hand me that sword. Keith Stuart

Staying in: Albums

Michael Kiwanuka - Fudge Out now Originally due for release last autumn, this fifth album from the Brit-nominated Kiwanuka was delayed after he suffered a haemorrhagic stroke after returning home from a tour. While his recovery continues, the self-produced Fudge is a reminder of his immense talents, as showcased on opener Summer Clothes’ gospel-tinged swirl.

Sasha Alex Sloan – And the Crowd Goes Mild Out now The Boston-born singer-songwriter, who’s co-written songs for the likes of Olivia Rodrigo, Charli xcx and Karol G, returns with her fourth album. As the title suggests, Sloan’s own songs veer towards the doleful, with singles Glitter and Empty pairing rich melodies with soothing soft-rock flourishes.

Claud - Me and the Music Out now Co-produced alongside John Congleton (Alvvays, St Vincent), Brooklyn-based Claud’s third album marks a shift in their mindset. While 2023’s lauded Supermodel took things very seriously, Me and the Music finds a lightness in a heavy world, especially on She Doesn’t Love Me’s effervescent indie jangle.

John Legend - Muse Out now After dabbling in music for children with 2024’s lullaby-centric My Favourite Dream, the Egot winner returns to more grownup themes on this entirely Pharrell-produced 11th album. The soulful Daylight is an upbeat love song, while the more politically focused Fireflies fuses jazz and gospel. MC

Staying in: Brain food

The One About Matthew Perry Netflix, 27 October A moving film recounting the life and career of the late Friends actor charting his rise to TV stardom and lifelong battles with addiction, as well as the tabloid scandals that accompanied his fame.

How Houdini Made Magic Podcast TV’s favourite illusionist Derren Brown tells the story of one of magic’s most iconic figures, Harry Houdini, in this 10-part series. Brown builds a fascinating picture of how Houdini fashioned himself a modern celebrity image.

3ETV Somerset House Channel London cultural institution Somerset House is celebrating the 10th anniversary of its experimental interdisciplinary Studios space with this diverse online channel featuring archived performance pieces, documentary shorts and new commissions. Ammar Kalia

article_text:
In den Filmen des Animationsstudios DreamWorks geht es häufig um Figuren, die nach dem Glück suchen und es durchaus auch finden, allerdings nicht so, wie sie es erwartet haben. So werden in „Forgotten Island“ (ab Donnerstag im Kino) zwei Schulabsolventinnen mit der Aussicht konfrontiert, in naher Zukunft nicht mehr alles miteinander zu teilen. Gut nur, dass nicht alles bleiben muss, wie es war, um bedeutsam zu bleiben.

Die Filme des Animationsstudios DreamWorks erzählen häufig von Figuren, die nach individuellem Glück streben und am Ende auch oft ein Happy End erfahren, dabei aber zugleich erleben, dass sich nicht immer alle Schwierigkeiten auflösen lassen. In „ Forgotten Island “ (ab 8.10. im Kino) geraten zwei Freundinnen auf eine magische Insel, wo ihre gemeinsamen Erinnerungen zu verblassen drohen. Damit würden Jo und Raissa genau das verlieren, was ihre Freundschaft über Jahre geprägt hat. Denn es sind ja gerade solche Erinnerungen, die Menschen verbinden. Dahinter steckt eine Angst, die vielen vertraut sein dürfte, wenn man nach dem letzten Schultag oder einem gemeinsamen Lebensabschnitt auseinandergeht und aus regelmäßigen Kontakten nur noch gelegentliche Besuche werden oder aus Freund:innen irgendwann bloße Bekannte. Die Animationsfilme von DreamWorks verhandeln oft solche schmerzhaften Erfahrungen des Erwachsenwerdens. Was bleibt, wenn sich die Umstände verändern oder das Leben voranschreitet?
